comments.author: pfdietz
comments.story: Declining quality of consumer-grade products – 2009 fridge compressor autopsy
comments.why: Compares original Mr. Coffee with modern drip makers and their simplification
comments.text: I just watched an amusing video that compares Mr. Coffee's original machine to modern drip coffeemakers. Mr. Coffee would cost $300 today (adjusted for inflation). There's been great simplification of the design over the years. [VIDEO] Given a more than order of magnitude reduction in price, a shorter lifespan can be tolerated, and could even be a rational consumer choice.

comments.author: RosanaAnaDana
comments.story: In the battle over the right to repair, open-source tractors offer alternatives
comments.why: Shows how modern drip makers gum up compared to Mr. Coffee
comments.text: [VIDEO] The specific mechanism that gums up the works occurs at 6:45. When you raise the lid of the modern version, grounds and coffee bits that have dusted up to the lid of the coffee maker drip via condensation into rear water reservoir. For greater detail, juxtapose minutes 8-11 with minutes 16-21. Mr. Coffee represents the king of drip still. And it is the greatest contributor to this fundamental design flaw (imp).
